best_for: People leaving Gmail or Outlook for encrypted email who are fine using Tuta's own apps instead of their usual mail client.
description:
Tuta Mail is the desktop app for Tuta, an email, calendar and contacts service from a German company that its founders Arne and Matthias started in 2011. Tuta says it stores customer data in Germany under the GDPR, runs on renewable energy and shows no ads.

The calendar sits right inside the mail app. You can send and answer meeting invites by email, set events that repeat, and get reminders on your phone without Google's push service, even on Android. Tuta says its encryption uses post-quantum methods, meant to hold up against future quantum computers. If you are leaving Gmail, you keep one place for mail and appointments without handing either to an ad company.

points.title: Encrypted by default
points.text: Mail, contacts and calendar are end-to-end encrypted, contacts' addresses included. Mail between Tuta users is encrypted automatically; to reach other people you can send a password-protected message.

points.title: Free plan: 1 GB and the basics
points.text: The free plan gives 1 GB of storage, one calendar and 3 labels. It has no custom domains, extra addresses, autoresponder, email import or support.

points.title: Log in or lose it
points.text: Free accounts are deleted after six months without a login. If you keep a free account as a backup address, sign in now and then.

points.title: Paid plans in euros
points.text: Revolutionary adds 20 GB, 15 extra addresses and 3 custom domains. Legend adds 500 GB and 10 domains. Both are priced in euros; check the pricing page, since a first-year discount was running when this was read.

points.title: Open source client
points.text: The desktop app is published on GitHub under GPL-3.0, so its code can be checked.

points.title: Install notes
points.text: The Windows installer comes as per-user and machine-wide versions, x64 only. The Mac app is a universal .dmg that needs macOS 13 or later. This site lists no Linux build.

points.title: Frequent releases on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 95 versions. macOS lists only the current release.
